title: Connection timed out - on high latency networks
body:
# Summary

When accessing any Streamlit app (e.g. https://covid19.multivacplatform.org/) from a low-latency network such as hughesnet  Satellite or a Verizon hotspot (e.g. >500 ms latency), I get “Please wait” then, after a while, a popup saying “Connection Error” - “Connection times out”.

Please see this post for more details- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/connection-timed-out/4091

# Steps to reproduce

What are the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Access a low-latency network
2. Go any the above streamlit url.

## Expected behavior:

The steamlit app should render as it normally does rather than timing out.

## Actual behavior:

Streamlit appears to connect but then timeout.

## Is this a regression?

No - however on low-latency (normal internet) the above and all streamlit sites work as expected.

# Debug info -

Not relevant since appear to happen to all steamlit apps, as far as I can tell.

# Additional information

If needed, add any other context about the problem here. For example, did this bug come from https://discuss.streamlit.io or another site? Link the original source here!

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-2312)

Hey [USER] I don't have a fast solution, but I believe the websocket needed to be allowed through the firewall in order to work. My guess is the VPN in blocking it.

Having this issue as well. End-users of our application are on satellite internet connections onboard ships, and as soon as they access the app once with a too-slow connection, the app is not useable until the cache is cleared completely. Even retrying from a stable land-based connection after getting the error does not work. Absolutely loving streamlit but this issue is a show stopper for us unfortunately... :(

For anyone having this issue, until [USER]'s MR is merged, you can directly patch your local Streamlit setup by modifying the minified JS file as follows (for `streamlit==0.83.0`):

```
sed -i -e 's/,1e3/,1e4/g' -e 's/,500/,10000/g' /usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.9cd30153.chunk.js
```

Which sets `WEBSOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS` and `PING_RETRY_PERIOD_MS` to 10s.

You are running the wrong command. The value $HASH changes with each python/streamlit version in `main.${HASH}.chunk.js`
The command below will for your specific version

`sed -i -e 's/,1e3/,1e4/g' -e 's/,500/,10000/g' /usr/local/lib/python3.*/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.*.chunk.js`

Hi all. 
I'm running into the same issue and [USER]'s snippet is not an option. Our app is deployed in a docker container in kubernetes and we don't have the permissions to run the sed command. 

I can see there are some discussions about adding a user option since several months ago. Is the subject still on course or was it abandoned ? 

Thanks.

[USER] you'd have to rebuild the container with the fix or otherwise mount the fixed file in the correct path.

I'm not sure I understand why this hasn't been fixed yet, it's been open for over two years and the fix is quite straightforward. Why are the latency times so short and why are they hardcoded in? In the real world, many global services have timeouts ranging from 1-3 minutes not 1 second or even 10 seconds.

**The default values are a huge issue**, especially when Streamlit apps are launched in containers and third party tools where the launch of the app itself can't be controlled via user configuration. We constantly have groups run into this issue when the app has a global audience. Latency is always high half way around the Earth. We either have to manually correct the javascript file in every single python virtual environment, for every single app, or simply tell them to stop using Streamlit because every other framework works fine.

I'm still hoping for a permanent out-of-the box fix for the defaults.

👍  Seconding the need for this. Ran into the same issue while trying to host a _streamlit_ app in k8s Google Cloud behind a corporate VPN. 

**Hot patching the package is a really ugly and maintainable fix when deploying the app to others**. 

Regardless, the commands above did not work for me with _streamlit_ `1.16.0` as they were excessively generic replacement and break the JS file. Here's what worked: 

```
sed -i -e 's/),1e3)/),1e4)/g' [PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.*.js

sed -i -e 's/baseUriPartsList,500/baseUriPartsList,10000/g' [PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.*.js
```

Adapt `[PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]` accordingly to the Python installation/environment you are working in.
